exposure: mode of delivery (elective cesarean section, emergency cesarean section, vacuum-assisted delivery, vaginal delivery)
outcome: failing initial otoacoustic emission (OAE) hearing screening (false-positive result)
cohort: The study included 5,621 infants with normal hearing, divided into a study group that failed the initial OAE screening and a control group that passed.
finding: Infants delivered by cesarean section or vacuum extraction have higher odds of failing the initial OAE screening when conducted within 48-72 hours after birth.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery significantly affected false-positive results, with elective cesarean section (OR 15.5), emergency cesarean section (OR 7.2), and vacuum delivery (OR 8.6) showing higher odds compared to vaginal delivery.
